title: A digitized book linked to its page regions (draft 0.1, 2026-11-05)
description: Three kinds of document share these definitions: a book's type list (format 'types'), one page's regions and units (format 'page'), and a whole book assembled from its pages (format 'book'). See schema/README.md. Rules that JSON Schema cannot express (references resolve, the units form a tree, types match) are checked by schema/book.py.

name.description: A type, flow or relation name.

unit_id.description: Page documents use local ids; a book document uses '<page id>#<local id>' of the unit's first fragment.

polygons.description: Outer rings in page-image pixel indices, largest piece first. Vertex (x, y) is the center of pixel column x and row y; in a corner-based system such as SVG, add 0.5 to both.

source.description: Provenance: which method, run, model or person produced this, and its raw evidence. Free-form.

description.description: What a unit of this type is in this book. Used in prompts.

role.description: Furniture (running headers, page numbers, margin line numbers) belongs to the page, not to any unit.

region.description: The book-neutral region class (method 037's types). A type with a class is printed as regions; a type without one is a container only.

flow.description: If set, units of this type may stand at the top level of this flow.

lang.description: Default BCP 47 language tag, such as sa-Deva or en.

numbered.description: Units of this type usually carry a printed number.

flows.description: Flow name to description. 'main' is the running text; others are, for example, 'notes'.

line.description: The page-level line id from the line finder. Two regions sharing a printed line have pieces with the same id.

text.description: The transcription of this line piece, as printed (see the book's conventions).

end.description: How this piece joins the next piece of the same unit: a space; a printed hyphen to drop (the word continues); no space (the word continues without a hyphen); or a line break to keep, as between verse lines.

type.description: A type from the book's type list: the type of the unit that owns this region, or a furniture type.

polygons.description: Where local processing fails, the model's box as a rectangle, recorded in source.

order.description: Reading order on the page, as given by the region step. Evidence only: the book's order is the order of the units.

label.description: The printed page number in ASCII digits, if known.

children.description: In reading order: the unit's own regions (of its own type) and its child units.

number.description: The printed number or marker, such as 25 for a verse or 3 for a footnote.

open.description: In a page document, start means the unit began on an earlier page and end that it goes on on a later page. A book document keeps these flags only for units still open at the edges of the pages it includes.

start.description: Character offset in the line piece's text.

marker.description: The printed marker, such as 3 or *.

flows.description: Flow name to its top-level units, in reading order.
